article_title: Civic Education Outcomes After Emergency Lockdowns: International Evidence from the COVID-19 Pandemic
citation: Kennedy, A. I., Mejía-Rodríguez, A. M., Strietholt, R. (2026). Civic Education Outcomes After Emergency Lockdowns: International Evidence from the COVID-19 Pandemic. Preprint submitted to Learning and Instruction. https://github.com/OxCGRT/covid-policy-dataset
title: OxCGRT stringency index and weighted school-closure duration measures
description: The study draws two explanatory measures from the Oxford COVID-19 Government Response Tracker (OxCGRT), a publicly available dataset collecting daily information on pandemic policy measures. The stringency index is described as "a continuous scale ranging from 0 (none of these measures are in place) to 100 (all policy measures are in place affecting the largest portion of the population possible)", averaged from January 2020 to February 2022. School-closure duration is a weighted sum of required closure days (weights 0 to 1 by geographic and sectoral scope), excluding weekends and academic holidays. These measures are combined with ICCS civic outcome scales in country-fixed-effects regressions.
requirements: Daily policy coding from OxCGRT combined with ICCS data for countries participating in both the 2016 and 2022 cycles
constraints: The two measures are positively correlated (r = 0.7) and are not used together in the same model due to multicollinearity
For the benchmarking participant (Germany's North Rhine-Westphalia), lockdown policies are measured at the national level rather than regional
examples: Sensitivity analyses compared alternative measures including the standard deviation of the stringency index, days above 50, a 'Fully closed' measure, and UIS-based closure durations (r = 0.89 with OxCGRT measures)
key_sources: Kennedy, A. I., Mejía-Rodríguez, A. M., Strietholt, R. (2026). Civic Education Outcomes After Emergency Lockdowns: International Evidence from the COVID-19 Pandemic. Preprint submitted to Learning and Instruction. https://github.com/OxCGRT/covid-policy-dataset

article_title: Using gesture recognition with the memory strategy to improve preschoolers’ learning performance, motor skills, and executive function
citation: Hsien-Sheng Hsiao, I-Hsiung Chang, Yi-Hsuan Chen, & Jyun-Chen Chen. (2025). Using gesture recognition with the memory strategy to improve preschoolers’ learning performance, motor skills, and executive function. Education Tech Research Dev, 73, 1791–1809. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10471-4
title: Four-step language learning memory strategy integrated into gesture-based physical learning activity
description: The study structures its learning activity around Oxford's (1990) memory strategy, whose "four steps of this memory strategy are: (1) creating mental linkages; (2) applying images and sounds; (3) reviewing; and (4) employing actions." Each step was implemented as a stage of the "Save the Prince/Princess" game, in which children used English knowledge, body movements, and memory to pass levels. The strategy was given to both the experimental and control groups, so the comparison isolates the gesture-recognition component.
requirements: An instructor delivering the four steps within themed English vocabulary lessons (Numbers, Fruits, Colors, and Animals)
constraints: The article states the four steps are suitable for integration into an interactive learning environment with gesture recognition
target_learners: preschoolers aged five to six learning English as a second language
examples: While teaching the word "Bird," the children were asked to discuss their image of birds and to perform like a bird
key_sources: Hsien-Sheng Hsiao, I-Hsiung Chang, Yi-Hsuan Chen, & Jyun-Chen Chen. (2025). Using gesture recognition with the memory strategy to improve preschoolers’ learning performance, motor skills, and executive function. Education Tech Research Dev, 73, 1791–1809. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10471-4

article_title: The Effect of Explicit Affective Strategy Training on Iranian EFL Learners' Oral Language Proficiency and Anxiety Reduction
citation: Fatemeh Mostafavi, Fereidoon Vahdany. (2016). The Effect of Explicit Affective Strategy Training on Iranian EFL learners' Oral Language Proficiency and Anxiety Reduction. Advances in Language and Literary Studies 7(4). https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.7n.4p.197
title: Oxford's (1990) taxonomy of affective strategies as an instructional framework for lowering anxiety and supporting oral language learning
description: The article applies Oxford's (1990) taxonomy of affective strategies — lowering your anxiety, encouraging yourself, and taking your emotional temperature — as the treatment framework, operationalized through relaxation exercises, music, humor, positive self-talk, risk-taking, feelings checklists and language learning journals. The article states that "affective strategies help learners gain control over their emotions, attitudes, and motivations". In this study the taxonomy supplied the explicit instruction content for the experimental group over six weeks.
requirements: Strategies must be made tangible through affect-based activities, since learning strategies are mental processes with limited discernable manifestations (Chamot, 1999, as cited in the article)
constraints: The article's evidence for the framework's effectiveness comes from one six-week study with 60 female high-school students in Tehran
target_learners: pre-intermediate EFL high school students, ages 16 to 18
target_learning_goals: anxiety reduction and emotional self-regulation in language learning
examples: The experimental group practiced Moskowitz's relaxation exercises, watched Mr. Bean humor videos, and completed guided weekly journals adapted from Nunan (1996) with sentence starters such as 'This week I studied:'
key_sources: Fatemeh Mostafavi, Fereidoon Vahdany. (2016). The Effect of Explicit Affective Strategy Training on Iranian EFL learners' Oral Language Proficiency and Anxiety Reduction. Advances in Language and Literary Studies 7(4). https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.7n.4p.197
